criteria.criterion: The firmware image executes on a NUCLEO-G070RB board.
criteria.observable: The board identity and the program counter reported by a connected debug probe
preconditions: A NUCLEO-G070RB board and a debug probe are available.
The firmware image has been built and programmed onto the board.
procedure: Confirm the board is identified as NUCLEO-G070RB.
Connect the debug probe and resume execution of the programmed firmware.
Sample the program counter twice while the MCU is running.
criteria.expected: The board is a NUCLEO-G070RB and the program counter advances between samples.

criteria.criterion: The default definition of LOGO_DISPLAY_MS in config.h is 2000, and the logo display timing uses that macro.
criteria.observable: The LOGO_DISPLAY_MS definition in config.h and the logo timing code's reference to LOGO_DISPLAY_MS
procedure: Inspect config.h for the default definition of LOGO_DISPLAY_MS.
Inspect the logo display timing code for use of LOGO_DISPLAY_MS.
criteria.expected: The default is 2000 ms and the logo display timing uses LOGO_DISPLAY_MS rather than a separate fixed duration.

criteria.criterion: config.h exposes configurable high-temperature and high-humidity thresholds for both demo and in-vehicle settings.
criteria.observable: The climate-threshold configuration entries in config.h
procedure: Inspect config.h for configurable high-temperature and high-humidity thresholds.
Read the configured values for demo and in-vehicle settings.
criteria.expected: Demo thresholds are 32 degC and 75%; in-vehicle thresholds are 45 degC and 80%.

criteria.criterion: config.h exposes configurable Z, X, +Y, and -Y ride-event thresholds for both demo and in-vehicle settings.
criteria.observable: The ride-event axis-threshold configuration entries in config.h
procedure: Inspect config.h for configurable Z, X, +Y, and -Y thresholds.
Read the configured values for demo and in-vehicle settings.
criteria.expected: Demo thresholds are Z = 0.30 g, X = 0.25 g, +Y = +0.25 g, and -Y = -0.25 g; each in-vehicle threshold is in the range 0.4–0.5 g, with the -Y threshold retaining its negative direction.

criteria.criterion: config.h exposes configurable sudden-window and event-display-time parameters with the specified durations.
criteria.observable: The sudden-window and event-display-time configuration entries in config.h
procedure: Inspect config.h for the sudden-window and event-display-time parameters.
Read their configured values.
criteria.expected: The sudden window is 100 ms and the event display time is 2 s.

criteria.criterion: The configured high-temperature threshold used by the firmware is 32 degC.
criteria.observable: The high-temperature threshold value in the firmware's shared configuration
procedure: Inspect the firmware configuration for the high-temperature threshold.
Confirm the value used by the firmware.
criteria.expected: 32 degC.

criteria.criterion: The configured high-humidity threshold used by the firmware is 75%.
criteria.observable: The high-humidity threshold value in the firmware's shared configuration
procedure: Inspect the firmware configuration for the high-humidity threshold.
Confirm the value used by the firmware.

criteria.criterion: A DHT22 acquisition uses PB4 and returns temperature and humidity matching the sensor's response.
criteria.observable: PB4 signal during acquisition and the firmware's returned temperature and humidity values
preconditions: A DHT22 is connected to PB4 and can provide a valid response.
procedure: Trigger a DHT22 acquisition.
Observe the acquisition signal on PB4 and record the sensor response.
Compare the firmware's returned temperature and humidity with the response.
criteria.expected: The acquisition signal is present on PB4, and both returned readings match the DHT22 response.

criteria.criterion: The I2C configuration assigns PB8 to SCL and PB9 to SDA for the bus used by both the MPU6050 and OLED.
criteria.observable: I2C pin configuration and the MPU6050 and OLED bus assignment in the source or build configuration
procedure: Inspect the I2C pin configuration.
Inspect the MPU6050 and OLED bus assignments.
criteria.expected: PB8 is configured as SCL, PB9 as SDA, and both devices are assigned to that same I2C bus.

criteria.criterion: Concurrent MPU6050 and OLED requests produce no overlapping I2C transactions, and both operations complete with their own expected results.
criteria.observable: Fake I2C transaction trace and the results returned by each operation
preconditions: The portable shared-bus access logic can be called with fake I2C callbacks.
MPU6050 and OLED operations use the same bus instance.
procedure: Start MPU6050 and OLED operations concurrently using distinct fake responses.
Record transaction entry and exit in the fake I2C callbacks.
Check the maximum number of simultaneously active transactions and each operation's result.
criteria.expected: The maximum number of active transactions is 1; both operations complete and each receives its own expected response.

criteria.criterion: DHT22 initialization and MPU6050 zeroing complete while the splash is active, and the splash ends at its configured deadline.
criteria.observable: Fake-clock timestamps for initialization, zeroing, and splash completion
preconditions: The splash is active in the portable application flow.
The configured splash duration and fake-clock hooks are available.
procedure: Start the splash with a fake clock and fake sensor operations.
Advance time through the configured splash duration.
Record when DHT22 initialization, MPU6050 zeroing, and splash completion occur.
criteria.expected: Both sensor operations complete after splash start and before splash completion; splash completion occurs at the configured duration, without an extension for sensor work.

criteria.criterion: The DHT22 read scheduler initiates consecutive reads 2000 ms apart.
criteria.observable: Fake-clock timestamps of DHT22 read initiation
preconditions: The DHT22 is initialized in the portable application logic.
The scheduler can be run with a fake clock.
procedure: Run the scheduler across at least three read periods using the fake clock.
Record each DHT22 read initiation time.
Calculate the difference between consecutive initiation times.
criteria.expected: Each consecutive initiation time differs by 2000 ms.

criteria.criterion: A successful DHT22 read publishes its temperature and humidity in the corresponding Celsius and percent fields.
criteria.observable: Published temperature and humidity fields after a fake successful DHT22 read
preconditions: The DHT22 read path can be supplied with fake sensor values.
procedure: Supply a successful fake read containing 23.5 °C and 48% humidity.
Run the read-and-publish path.
Inspect the published temperature and humidity fields.
criteria.expected: The temperature field is 23.5 °C and the humidity field is 48%.

criteria.criterion: The MPU6050 configuration selects the ±4 g accelerometer range.
criteria.observable: Accelerometer configuration register value written by the MPU6050 driver
preconditions: The MPU6050 driver can be called with fake I2C register callbacks.
procedure: Initialize the MPU6050 using the driver.
Capture the accelerometer configuration register write.
Decode the full-scale selection bits.
criteria.expected: The full-scale selection is ±4 g (FS_SEL = 1).

criteria.criterion: The MPU6050 sampling logic requests acceleration samples at 100 Hz.
criteria.observable: Fake-clock timestamps of successive acceleration sample requests
preconditions: The portable MPU6050 sampling logic can be run with a fake clock and fake I2C callbacks.
The MPU6050 is initialized.
procedure: Run the sampling logic through several sample periods with the fake clock.
Record successive acceleration sample request times.
criteria.expected: Successive requests are separated by 10 ms (100 samples per second).
criteria.rationale: The stated sample rate is 100 Hz, whose period is 1/100 second, or 10 ms; the fake clock isolates the sampling policy from MCU scheduling jitter.

criteria.criterion: Each acceleration axis is converted from raw MPU6050 counts to g using the configured ±4 g scale.
criteria.observable: Converted X, Y, and Z acceleration values from known raw sample counts
preconditions: The MPU6050 conversion logic can be called with known raw samples.
The ±4 g range is configured.
procedure: Provide raw axis counts corresponding to 1 g at the ±4 g setting (8192 counts on one axis and zero on the others).
Run the acceleration conversion.
Inspect the converted X, Y, and Z values.
criteria.expected: The axis supplied with 8192 counts is 1.0 g, and the other two axes are 0.0 g, subject to the implementation's numeric representation precision.
criteria.rationale: The standard MPU6050 sensitivity at the ±4 g setting is 8192 LSB/g; checking this conversion verifies that raw readings are presented in g rather than counts.

criteria.criterion: After one second of flat-and-still calibration samples, the calibrated acceleration is X = 0 g, Y = 0 g, and Z = 1 g.
criteria.observable: Calibrated X, Y, and Z acceleration values after the calibration routine completes
preconditions: The calibration routine can be called with injected acceleration samples and a fake clock.
Injected samples represent a flat, still board for one second, with gravity on Z.
procedure: Start calibration and provide flat-and-still samples for one second.
Allow the calibration routine to complete.
Read the calibrated X, Y, and Z values.
criteria.expected: X = 0 g, Y = 0 g, and Z = 1 g.

criteria.criterion: The first sensor screen becomes the active screen when the configured splash completes, and it presents the calibrated X, Y, and Z values as valid.
criteria.observable: Application screen state and displayed sensor values and validity state after splash completion
preconditions: The application flow can be run with a fake clock and fake calibrated MPU6050 data.
Calibration has completed during the splash.
procedure: Run the application through splash completion with valid calibrated values X = 0 g, Y = 0 g, Z = 1 g.
Inspect the active screen and its sensor values immediately after the splash transition.
criteria.expected: The active screen is the first sensor screen, and it presents valid values X = 0 g, Y = 0 g, Z = 1 g.

criteria.criterion: The displayed acceleration values are assigned to lateral X, longitudinal Y, and vertical Z axes.
criteria.observable: Axis labels or axis fields consumed by the display path after supplying distinct X, Y, and Z values
preconditions: The portable display-data mapping can be called with distinct acceleration values.
procedure: Supply distinct X, Y, and Z acceleration values to the display mapping.
Inspect the values assigned to the lateral, longitudinal, and vertical display fields.
criteria.expected: Lateral uses X, longitudinal uses Y, and vertical uses Z.

criteria.criterion: The event-processing inputs use X for lateral cornering, Y for longitudinal acceleration/braking, and Z for vertical bumps.
criteria.observable: Axis values delivered to the event-processing logic after supplying distinct X, Y, and Z values
preconditions: The portable event-input mapping can be called with distinct acceleration values.
procedure: Supply distinct X, Y, and Z acceleration values to the event-input mapping.
Inspect the values delivered to the lateral, longitudinal, and vertical event inputs.
criteria.expected: Lateral event input uses X, longitudinal event input uses Y, and vertical event input uses Z.

criteria.criterion: A failed DHT22 or MPU6050 acquisition is marked invalid and is not presented as a valid displayed measurement.
criteria.observable: Acquisition validity state and displayed measurement state after injecting each sensor failure
preconditions: The portable acquisition and display logic can be exercised with fake sensor callbacks that report failure.
procedure: Inject a failed DHT22 acquisition and inspect its validity and display state.
Inject a failed MPU6050 acquisition and inspect its validity and display state.
criteria.expected: For each failed acquisition, the result is invalid and is not presented as a valid measurement.

criteria.criterion: A failed DHT22 or MPU6050 acquisition does not cause an event to be triggered from that failed result.
criteria.observable: Event-detection inputs and event outputs after injecting each sensor failure
preconditions: The portable acquisition-to-event path can be exercised with fake sensor callbacks that report failure.
procedure: Inject a failed DHT22 acquisition and run event processing.
Inject a failed MPU6050 acquisition and run event processing.
Inspect the event inputs and emitted event outputs for each case.
criteria.expected: Failed-result values are excluded from event-detection inputs, and neither injected failure triggers an event from those values.

criteria.criterion: The display configuration selects the SH1106 driver and assigns I2C SCL to PB8 and SDA to PB9 on the bus also used by the MPU6050.
criteria.observable: Display-driver selection and I2C pin/device assignments in the firmware configuration and initialization code
procedure: Inspect the display driver selection and I2C initialization.
Inspect the MPU6050 bus assignment.
criteria.expected: SH1106 selected; SCL=PB8; SDA=PB9; the display and MPU6050 use the same I2C bus.

criteria.criterion: The display component specification identifies a 1.3-inch OLED.
criteria.observable: OLED entry in the project parts list or display specification
procedure: Inspect the project parts list or display specification.
criteria.expected: Display diagonal is 1.3 in.
criteria.rationale: The requirement and its expected value specify the physical display diagonal, which can be checked against the component specification but not established by a firmware unit test.

criteria.criterion: The logo.h asset declares a flash-resident 1-bit bitmap containing 1024 bytes in SH1106 page order.
criteria.observable: Bitmap declaration, storage qualifier, and array size in logo.h
procedure: Inspect logo.h and count or evaluate the declared bitmap array length.
criteria.expected: A const/flash-resident bitmap array with 8 × 128 = 1024 bytes, each byte representing one page column.

criteria.criterion: The logo asset definition specifies that each byte's least-significant bit maps to the top row of its 8-pixel page.
criteria.observable: Bitmap-format documentation or bit-mapping definition adjacent to the logo asset
procedure: Inspect the logo format definition or documentation in logo.h.
criteria.expected: Bit 0 maps to the top row, and the asset dimensions are 128 columns by 8 pages (128×64 pixels).

criteria.criterion: The splash rendering code places the 124×26 logo at coordinates that center it within a 128×64 display.
criteria.observable: Logo draw call dimensions and x/y coordinates in the splash rendering code
preconditions: The splash rendering implementation is present.
procedure: Inspect the splash draw call and its coordinate calculations.
criteria.expected: Logo dimensions are 124×26 pixels and its top-left coordinate is x=2, y=19.

criteria.criterion: The splash renderer clears the display to black and draws the logo as white pixels without scaling or inversion.
criteria.observable: Splash framebuffer clear and logo pixel-rendering operations
preconditions: The splash rendering implementation is present.
procedure: Inspect the framebuffer clear value and the logo pixel-rendering path.
criteria.expected: Background and border pixels are black; set logo bits render white; source bitmap coordinates map one-to-one to display pixels.

criteria.criterion: The splash elapsed-time check uses HAL_GetTick and contains no blocking delay call.
criteria.observable: Splash timing code and delay calls in the splash path
procedure: Inspect the splash timing implementation and its call path.
criteria.expected: Elapsed time is determined using HAL_GetTick; no blocking delay is used to hold the splash.

criteria.criterion: While the splash state is active, processing an alert does not add an alert to the rendered display and does not command the LED to blink.
criteria.observable: Fake display output and fake LED command history after exercising the splash-state logic
preconditions: The portable splash/application logic can be called with fake display and LED interfaces.
procedure: Enter the splash state.
Inject an alert and advance the application logic through the splash interval.
Inspect the fake display output and LED command history.
criteria.expected: No alert message is rendered, and no blink command or blinking LED state is produced during the splash interval.

criteria.criterion: The SH1106 driver adds two columns to the starting column for writes that render both the logo and a non-logo screen.
criteria.observable: Captured column-address command bytes from a fake SH1106 I/O interface
preconditions: The SH1106 driver can be called with a fake I/O interface.
procedure: Render the logo through the driver and capture its column-address command.
Render a non-logo screen through the driver and capture its column-address command.
criteria.expected: For each rendered screen, the driver uses visible column c at SH1106 RAM column c+2; the offset is applied exactly once.

criteria.criterion: When an event is processed, the next rendered screen contains its message and retains the current temperature and humidity values.
criteria.observable: Rendered display text or framebuffer from the portable screen-rendering logic
preconditions: The portable event and display logic can be called with temperature and humidity values.
procedure: Set known temperature and humidity values.
Process an event with a known message.
Render the screen and inspect its text or framebuffer.
criteria.expected: The event message and both previously supplied temperature and humidity values are present in the rendered screen.

criteria.criterion: The event message is included in the first display update generated after the event is processed.
criteria.observable: Display update sequence and rendered contents from the portable application logic
preconditions: The portable application logic exposes display updates to a fake display interface.
procedure: Set known temperature and humidity values.
Process an event and capture the first subsequent display update.
criteria.expected: The first display update after event processing contains the event message.
criteria.rationale: The statement says the message appears immediately, but gives no numeric latency bound; this criterion interprets immediate as appearing on the first display update after event processing rather than inventing a time threshold.

criteria.criterion: After the splash transition, the rendered screen is titled Vehicle Parameters and includes DHT22 temperature in degC, DHT22 humidity in %, and X, Y, and Z acceleration values with g shown for Z.
criteria.observable: Rendered screen text or framebuffer from the portable screen-rendering logic
preconditions: The portable renderer can be called with known DHT22 and MPU6050 readings.
procedure: Provide distinct known temperature, humidity, and X/Y/Z values.
Render the post-splash sensor screen.
Inspect the title, values, and unit text.
criteria.expected: The screen contains the title Vehicle Parameters, the supplied temperature with degC, the supplied humidity with %, the supplied X/Y/Z values, and g for Z.

criteria.criterion: The first sensor screen following the splash renders valid zero values for X, Y, and Z when the initial acceleration values are zero.
criteria.observable: Rendered X/Y/Z fields from the portable startup and screen-rendering logic
preconditions: The portable startup logic can be driven through splash completion with initial acceleration values set to zero.
procedure: Initialize X, Y, and Z acceleration values to zero.
Advance the startup logic past the splash.
Inspect the first sensor screen.
criteria.expected: The first sensor screen displays valid zero readings for X, Y, and Z.

criteria.criterion: The SH1106 interface is initialized before the first logo display write, and the logo becomes visible within 100 ms of power-up.
criteria.observable: I2C bus trace showing initialization and first logo write, plus the OLED's visible logo onset measured from power-up
preconditions: NUCLEO-G070RB and the SH1106 OLED are connected and powered.
A bus analyzer and a means to measure power-up-to-visible-logo time are available.
procedure: Capture the I2C bus and power-up timing while powering the board.
Identify the SH1106 initialization sequence and first logo write.
Measure the time from power-up to visible logo.
criteria.expected: Initialization precedes the first logo write, and visible logo onset is no later than 100 ms after power-up.

criteria.criterion: On power-up, the logo becomes visible within 100 ms, remains the displayed content for 1.9–2.1 seconds, and precedes any sensor data or heading.
criteria.observable: OLED output recorded from power-up through splash completion, with timestamps
preconditions: NUCLEO-G070RB and the SH1106 OLED are connected and powered.
A recording or instrument can observe OLED output and timestamp power-up.
procedure: Power up the board while recording the OLED output and timing.
Measure logo onset and duration.
Check the display contents from power-up until the logo disappears.
criteria.expected: Logo onset is at or before 100 ms; logo duration is 1.9–2.1 s; no sensor data or heading appears before the logo.

criteria.criterion: After splash completion, the OLED changes to the Vehicle Parameters screen, and resetting during normal operation causes the logo splash to play again.
criteria.observable: OLED output recorded across splash completion and across a reset during normal operation
preconditions: NUCLEO-G070RB and the SH1106 OLED are connected and powered.
procedure: Power up and observe the screen after the splash ends.
Allow the Vehicle Parameters screen to appear, then reset the board.
Observe the OLED output after reset.
criteria.expected: The post-splash screen is Vehicle Parameters; after reset, the logo is displayed again before the normal screen.

criteria.criterion: The Vehicle Parameters renderer labels the acceleration readings exactly X:, Y:, and Z:, and appends the exact suffix ' g' to the Z value.
criteria.observable: Rendered screen text or framebuffer from the portable Vehicle Parameters renderer
preconditions: The portable Vehicle Parameters renderer can be called with known acceleration values.
procedure: Render the Vehicle Parameters screen with distinct X, Y, and Z values.
Inspect the rendered labels and Z-value suffix.
criteria.expected: The acceleration labels are exactly X:, Y:, and Z:, and the Z value is followed by ' g'.

criteria.criterion: When the displayed temperature is greater than its configured high limit, the OLED shows an exclamation mark adjacent to the temperature value.
criteria.observable: Temperature text and adjacent marker on the OLED
preconditions: Temperature has been read.
The OLED is initialized and displaying the temperature.
procedure: In demo mode, set the temperature above 32 °C and observe the OLED.
In in-vehicle mode, set the temperature above 45 °C and observe the OLED.
criteria.expected: In each mode, the temperature value is displayed with an adjacent "!" while it is above that mode's configured limit.

criteria.criterion: When the displayed humidity is greater than its configured high limit, the OLED shows an exclamation mark adjacent to the humidity value.
criteria.observable: Humidity text and adjacent marker on the OLED
preconditions: Humidity has been read.
The OLED is initialized and displaying the humidity.
procedure: In demo mode, set the humidity above 75% and observe the OLED.
In in-vehicle mode, set the humidity above 80% and observe the OLED.
criteria.expected: In each mode, the humidity value is displayed with an adjacent "!" while it is above that mode's configured limit.

criteria.criterion: A change meeting the associated event threshold and arriving exactly 100 ms after the baseline sample is detected as an event.
criteria.observable: Event-detection function result or event state after processing the sample pair
preconditions: The event detector is callable with injected acceleration samples and timestamps.
The associated event threshold is configured.
procedure: Provide a baseline acceleration sample at time t.
Provide a sample with the associated-axis change at least equal to the configured threshold at t + 100 ms.
Read the event-detection result or event state.
criteria.expected: The qualifying event is detected.

criteria.criterion: A change meeting the associated event threshold but arriving more than 100 ms after the baseline sample is not detected as a change within the configured sudden-change window.
criteria.observable: Event-detection function result or event state after processing the sample pair
preconditions: The event detector is callable with injected acceleration samples and timestamps.
The associated event threshold is configured.
procedure: Provide a baseline acceleration sample at time t.
Provide a sample with the associated-axis change at least equal to the configured threshold at a time greater than t + 100 ms.
Read the event-detection result or event state.
criteria.expected: The sample pair does not trigger detection based on the 100 ms window.
criteria.rationale: The verification method is Test and the acceptance criterion defines a 100 ms window; checking a just-outside-window sample distinguishes the stated bound from an unbounded threshold-crossing detector.

criteria.criterion: A Z-axis change of at least 0.30 g identifies an Unseen SpeedBreaker in demo mode.
criteria.observable: Identified event type returned by the event detector
preconditions: The detector is callable with injected, zeroed acceleration samples.
Demo thresholds are selected.
procedure: Provide a zeroed baseline sample.
Within 100 ms, provide a sample whose Z-axis change is 0.30 g or greater.
Read the identified event type.
criteria.expected: The identified event type is Unseen SpeedBreaker.

criteria.criterion: An X-axis change of at least 0.25 g identifies a Wide Turn in demo mode.
criteria.observable: Identified event type returned by the event detector
preconditions: The detector is callable with injected, zeroed acceleration samples.
Demo thresholds are selected.
procedure: Provide a zeroed baseline sample.
Within 100 ms, provide a sample whose X-axis change is 0.25 g or greater.
Read the identified event type.
criteria.expected: The identified event type is Wide Turn.

criteria.criterion: A positive Y-axis change of at least 0.25 g identifies Speeding in demo mode.
criteria.observable: Identified event type returned by the event detector
preconditions: The detector is callable with injected, zeroed acceleration samples.
Demo thresholds are selected.
procedure: Provide a zeroed baseline sample.
Within 100 ms, provide a sample with a positive Y-axis change of at least 0.25 g.
Read the identified event type.
criteria.expected: The identified event type is Speeding.

criteria.criterion: A negative Y-axis change with magnitude at least 0.25 g identifies Sudden Braking in demo mode.
criteria.observable: Identified event type returned by the event detector
preconditions: The detector is callable with injected, zeroed acceleration samples.
Demo thresholds are selected.
procedure: Provide a zeroed baseline sample.
Within 100 ms, provide a sample with a negative Y-axis change of magnitude at least 0.25 g.
Read the identified event type.
criteria.expected: The identified event type is Sudden Braking.

criteria.criterion: Each in-vehicle event threshold is configurable within its stated 0.4–0.5 g range.
criteria.observable: Configured in-vehicle thresholds for Z, X, positive Y, and negative Y event detection
preconditions: In-vehicle configuration is selected.
The event-threshold configuration can be read.
procedure: Read the configured Z, X, positive Y, and negative Y thresholds.
Check each threshold against the stated range.
criteria.expected: Each of the four configured thresholds is between 0.4 g and 0.5 g, inclusive.

criteria.criterion: The LD4 control configuration maps the LED output to GPIO PA5.
criteria.observable: GPIO configuration and LD4 pin mapping in the source or board configuration
preconditions: The firmware source or board configuration is available for review.
procedure: Inspect the LD4 pin mapping and GPIO initialization configuration.
Confirm the configured LD4 output pin is PA5.
criteria.expected: LD4 is controlled through PA5.

criteria.criterion: While an event alert is active, LD4 has 500 ms on intervals alternating with 500 ms off intervals.
criteria.observable: LD4 output waveform on GPIO PA5
preconditions: An event alert is active.
LD4 is connected through PA5.
A logic analyzer or equivalent instrument is attached to PA5.
procedure: Trigger an event alert.
Capture the PA5 waveform for multiple blink cycles.
Measure consecutive high and low intervals.
criteria.expected: Each on interval is 500 ms and each following off interval is 500 ms, producing a 1 Hz cycle.

criteria.criterion: After the last event, the OLED continues showing the event message until the 2-second post-event interval ends, then clears the message.
criteria.observable: Event message on the OLED after the last event
preconditions: At least one event has occurred.
The OLED is displaying the event message.
procedure: Record the time of the last event.
Observe the OLED before 2 seconds have elapsed.
Observe the OLED at the 2-second post-event deadline.
criteria.expected: The event message remains displayed before the 2-second deadline and is no longer displayed at the deadline.

criteria.criterion: After the last event, LD4 continues blinking until the 2-second post-event interval ends, then stops blinking.
criteria.observable: LD4 output waveform on GPIO PA5 after the last event
preconditions: At least one event has occurred.
LD4 is connected through PA5.
A logic analyzer or equivalent instrument is attached to PA5.
procedure: Record the time of the last event.
Observe PA5 before 2 seconds have elapsed.
Continue observing PA5 through the 2-second post-event deadline.
criteria.expected: Blinking continues before the 2-second deadline and ceases at the deadline.

criteria.criterion: When multiple listed events are active simultaneously, the selected event message is the highest-priority active event in the specified order.
criteria.observable: Selected event message or event-priority result produced by the event presentation logic
preconditions: The event-priority logic is callable with injected active-event states.
At least two listed event states can be made active simultaneously.
procedure: For each pair or combination of listed events, mark the events active simultaneously.
Read the selected event message or priority result.
criteria.expected: Sudden Braking is selected over Unseen SpeedBreaker, Wide Turn, and Speeding; Unseen SpeedBreaker is selected over Wide Turn and Speeding; and Wide Turn is selected over Speeding.

criteria.criterion: The dashboard receives and makes available both cabin-comfort data and ride data from the firmware during operation.
criteria.observable: The dashboard's received data or display showing cabin-comfort and ride data
preconditions: The device is installed in a vehicle.
The dashboard is connected and able to receive the firmware's stream.
procedure: Power the device and dashboard.
Operate the system while observing the dashboard's received data or display.
Confirm that both cabin-comfort data and ride data are available on the dashboard.
criteria.expected: Both cabin-comfort data and ride data from the firmware are available at the dashboard.
